verses.zh: （大卫的诗，交与伶长。）耶和华啊，王必因你的能力欢喜；因你的救恩，他的快乐何其大！
verses.en: For the music director, a psalm of David.O Lord, the king rejoices in the strength you give;[NOTE:1] he takes great delight in the deliverance you provide.[NOTE:2]
notes: Psalm 21. The psalmist praises the Lord for the way he protects and blesses the Davidic king.
Heb “in your strength.” The translation interprets the pronominal suffix as subjective, rather than merely descriptive (or attributive).
verses.commentary:
21:1 Note the synonymous parallelism between
"in Your strength" and "in Your salvation."

The term (BDB 447, FEMININE SINGULAR)
translated salvation has several possible connotations.

- prosperity – Job 30:15

- deliverance/help – 2 Sam. 10:11; 1 Chr. 19:12; Ps. 22:1

- salvation – Gen. 49:18; Ps. 3:2,8; 14:7; 35:3; 53:6; 62:2; and many more

- victory – Exod. 15:2; Ps. 20:6; 21:1,5; 44:4; 68:20-21; 118:14,15,21

YHWH is our great hope and there is no other! In light of this, faithful
followers (in this context, the King) will continue to

- be glad – BDB 970, KB 1330, Qal IMPERFECT, cf. Ps. 9:2

- rejoice – BDB 162, KB 189, Qal IMPERFECT, cf. Ps. 9:14

SPECIAL TOPIC: SALVATION (OT term)

▣ "O Lord" This is the covenant name for Israel's God, from
the VERB "to be."

SPECIAL TOPIC: NAMES FOR DEITY, D.

verses.zh: 他心里所愿的，你已经赐给他；他嘴唇所求的，你未尝不应允。（细拉）
verses.en: You grant[NOTE:1] him his heart’s desire;you do not refuse his request.[NOTE:2] (Selah)
notes: Heb “and in your deliverance, how greatly he rejoices.”

The translation assumes the perfect verbal forms in v. 2 are generalizing, stating factually what God typically does for the king. Another option is to take them as present perfects, “you have granted…you have not refused.” See v. 4, which mentions a specific request for a long reign.
verses.commentary:
21:2 This verse seems to link to Ps. 20:4
and is connected to the King's prayer for military victory.

Notice the two parallel PERFECT VERBS (i.e., completed action).

- has given – BDB 678, KB 733, Qal PERFECT

- has not withheld — BDB 586, KB 602, negated, Qal PERFECT

▣

NASB, NKJV, NET, NRSV, Peshitta
"request"

NJB
"prayer"

LXX
"wish"

NEB
"ask"

The word (BDB 77, KB 92) is found only here in the OT. It seems, in
context, to refer to a ritual liturgical prayer before a battle, possibly
in the tabernacle/temple.

Remember, for words only used once in the OT (hapax legomena), there are
only so many ways to seek its meaning/connotation.

- the main truth of the strophe

- Hebrew parallelism

- relate cognate roots from other Semitic languages from the same period

- context, context, context; words have meaning only in contexts

▣ "Selah" See note at Ps.
3:2 and the Introduction to Psalms, VII. Some commentators feel it denotes a
point in the liturgy where there is a transition to another liturgical act
(i.e., praise, song, sacrifice, another liturgy read, bowing, etc.).

verses.zh: 你以美福迎接他，把精金的冠冕戴在他头上。
verses.en: For you bring him[NOTE:1] rich[NOTE:2] blessings;[NOTE:3] you place a golden crown on his head.
notes: Heb “and the request of his lips you do not refuse.”
Or “meet him [with].”
Heb “good.”
verses.commentary:
21:3-6 These are the actions of YHWH on behalf of the King.

- meet him with the blessings of good things (i.e., YHWH Himself welcomes the victorious king)

- set a crown of fine gold on his head (i.e., a reaffirmation of kingship or the liturgical transfer
of the battle helmet for the royal crown)

- gave him his prayer for life (i.e., victory in battle)

- placed upon him

- splendor (BDB 217, KB 241)

- majesty (BDB 214, KB 240) – these are descriptions of YHWH (cf. 1 Chr. 16:27; Ps. 45:3; 96:6;
104:1; 111:3), but because of YHWH's image in mankind (cf. Gen. 1:26-27), they share these attributes (cf. Ps. 8:5)

- make him blessed for a long life

- ‘olam must be interpreted in context, see

SPECIAL TOPIC: FOREVER

- a literary parallel would be "long live the king," cf. 1 Sam. 10:24; 1 Kgs. 1:25,31,34,39; Dan. 2:4; 3:9

- make him joyful in Your presence (this would denote temple worship)

It is not just the King who is the recipient of YHWH's actions, but
through him all the covenant people.

▣ "forever" See same root (BDB 723 I) in v. 5.

verses.zh: 他向你求寿，你便赐给他，就是日子长久，直到永远。
verses.en: He asked you to sustain his life,[NOTE:1] and you have granted him long life and an enduring dynasty.[NOTE:2]
notes: You bring him rich blessings. The following context indicates that God’s “blessings” include deliverance/protection, vindication, sustained life, and a long, stable reign (see also Pss 3:8; 24:5).
Heb “life he asked from you.” Another option is to translate the perfect verbal forms in v. 4 with the present tense, “he asks…you grant.”

verses.zh: 他因你的救恩大有荣耀；你又将尊荣威严加在他身上。
verses.en: Your deliverance brings him great honor;[NOTE:1] you give him majestic splendor.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “you have granted him length of days forever and ever.” The phrase “length of days,” when used of human beings, usually refers to a lengthy period of time (such as one’s lifetime). See, for example, Deut 30:20; Job 12:12; Ps 91:16; Prov 3:2, 16; Lam 5:20. The additional phrase “forever and ever” is hyperbolic. While it seems to attribute eternal life to the king (see Pss 61:6-7; 72:5 as well), the underlying reality is the king’s enduring dynasty. He will live on, as it were, through his descendants, who will continue to rule over his kingdom long after he has passed off the scene.
Or “great glory.”

verses.zh: 你使他有洪福，直到永远，又使他在你面前欢喜快乐。
verses.en: For you grant him lasting blessings;you give him great joy by allowing him into your presence.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “majesty and splendor you place upon him.” For other uses of the phrase הוֹד וְהָדָר (hod vehadar, “majesty and splendor”) see 1 Chr 16:27; Job 40:10; Pss 96:6; 104:1; 111:3.

verses.zh: 王倚靠耶和华，因至高者的慈爱必不摇动。
verses.en: For the king trusts[NOTE:1] in the Lord,and because of the Most High’s[NOTE:2] faithfulness he is not shaken.[NOTE:3]
notes: Heb “you make him happy with joy with [i.e., “close by” or “in”] your face.” On the idiom “with your face” (i.e., “in your presence”) see Ps 16:11 and BDB 816 s.v. פָּנֻה II.2.a.
The active participle draws attention to the ongoing nature of the action.
The divine title “Most High” (עֶלְיוֹן, ʿelyon) pictures God as the exalted ruler of the universe who vindicates the innocent and judges the wicked. Note the focus of vv. 8-12 and see Ps 47:2.
verses.commentary:
21:7 "the king trusts in the Lord" This is an affirmation of the
king's faith orientation (BDB 105, KB 120, Qal active
participle, cf. Ps. 4:5; 9:10; 13:5; 22:4,5,9; and many more). The
king has strength, joy, and deliverance only through YHWH.

▣ "the lovingkindness of the Most High"
The special covenant term, "lovingkindness" (hesed, BDB
338, see

SPECIAL TOPIC: LOVINGKINDNESS) means YHWH's covenant loyalty. YHWH is
always faithful, the King and the nation will be also, if they continue to
"trust" (BDB 105, KB 120) in Him (cf. Ps. 125:1).

Nehemiah 9 is
a record of YHWH's faithfulness and Israel's unfaithfulness!

For "Most High" (Elyon, BDB 751) see

SPECIAL TOPIC: NAMES FOR DEITY, B.

▣

NASB, LXX, JPSOA
"he will not be shaken"

NKJV, NRSV, Peshitta
"he shall not be moved"

TEV
"he will always be secure"

NJB
"will keep him from falling"

The VERB (BDB 556, KB 555, Niphal IMPERFECT)
means "totter," "shake," or "slip." It can be used in several senses.

- place on the throne

- security in life

- godly lifestyle

To see the different senses see Ps. 10:6; 15:5; 16:8; 21:7; 30:6; 62:2,6;
112:6; Prov. 10:30; 12:3. There is stability in YHWH but not in a fallen
world.

verses.zh: 你的手要搜出你的一切仇敌；你的右手要搜出那些恨你的人。
verses.en: You[NOTE:1] prevail over[NOTE:2] all your enemies;your power is too great for those who hate you.[NOTE:3]
notes: Another option is to translate the imperfect verbal form as future, “he will not be shaken” (cf. NRSV “he shall not be moved”). Even if one chooses this option, the future tense must be understood in a generalizing sense.

The king is now addressed. One could argue that the Lord is still being addressed, but v. 9 militates against this proposal, for there the Lord is mentioned in the third person and appears to be distinct from the addressee (unless, of course, one takes “Lord” in v. 9 as vocative; see the note on “them” in v. 9b). Verse 7 begins this transition to a new addressee by referring to both the king and the Lord in the third person (in vv. 1-6 the Lord is addressed and only the king referred to in the third person).

Heb “your hand finds.” The idiom pictures the king grabbing hold of his enemies and defeating them (see 1 Sam 23:17). The imperfect verbal forms in vv. 8-12 may be translated with the future tense, as long as the future is understood as generalizing.
verses.commentary:
21:8-12 These verses describe what YHWH
(i.e., through the king's army) will do if the king and people stay
faithful.

- power over your enemies

- your enemies will be destroyed (see

SPECIAL TOPIC: FIRE)

- your enemies and their descendants will be cut off and disappear

- your enemies will not succeed in their plans (i.e., to plan against YHWH's king
and covenant people is to plan against Him, cf. Ps. 21:11a; Ps. 2:1-3; 83:1-5)

- your enemies will retreat in battle

Some scholars (AB) see these verses as describing YHWH's actions in battle
on behalf of His covenant king and people (i.e., YHWH as the Divine Warrior, Holy War imagery).

▣ "hand" This is a Hebrew
idiom of the power to act.

SPECIAL
TOPIC: HAND.

verses.zh: 你发怒的时候，要使他们如在炎热的火炉中。耶和华要在他的震怒中吞灭他们；那火要把他们烧尽了。
verses.en: You burn them up like a fiery furnace[NOTE:1] when you appear.[NOTE:2] The Lord angrily devours them;[NOTE:3] the fire consumes them.
notes: Heb “your right hand finds those who hate you.”

Heb “you make them like a furnace of fire.” Although many modern translations retain the literal Hebrew, the statement is elliptical. The point is not that he makes them like a furnace, but like an object burned in a furnace (cf. NEB, “at your coming you shall plunge them into a fiery furnace”).
Heb “at the time of your face.” The “face” of the king here refers to his angry presence. See Lam 4:16.
verses.commentary:
21:9 "The Lord will swallow them up"
This VERB (BDB 118, KB 134, Piel IMPERFECT) is an
idiom for complete destruction (cf. Job 2:3; 10:8; Lam. 2:2,5,8). Sheol was personified
as an animal which swallows people (cf. Num. 16:30; Prov. 1:12; Isa. 5:14; Hab. 2:5).

21:12a This imagery is used of troops fleeing in disarray and defeat. They have
turned their backs to YHWH's covenant army and king.

verses.zh: 你必从世上灭绝他们的子孙（原文是果子），从人间灭绝他们的后裔。
verses.en: You destroy their offspring[NOTE:1] from the earth,their descendants[NOTE:2] from among the human race.[NOTE:3]
notes: Heb “the Lord, in his anger he swallows them, and fire devours them.” Some take “the Lord” as a vocative, in which case he is addressed in vv. 8-9a. But this makes the use of the third person in v. 9b rather awkward, though the king could be the subject (see vv. 1-7).
Heb “fruit.” The next line makes it clear that offspring is in view.
Heb “seed.”

verses.zh: 因为他们有意加害于你；他们想出计谋，却不能做成。
verses.en: Yes,[NOTE:1] they intend to do you harm;[NOTE:2] they dream up a scheme,[NOTE:3] but they do not succeed.[NOTE:4]
notes: Heb “sons of man.”
Or “for.”

Heb “they extend against you harm.” The perfect verbal forms in v. 11 are taken as generalizing, stating factually what the king’s enemies typically do. Another option is to translate with the past tense (“they intended…planned”).
See Ps 10:2.

verses.zh: 你必使他们转背逃跑，向他们的脸搭箭在弦。
verses.en: For you make them retreat[NOTE:1] when you aim your arrows at them.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “they lack ability.”
Heb “you make them a shoulder,” i.e., “you make them turn and run, showing the back of their neck and shoulders.”

verses.zh: 耶和华啊，愿你因自己的能力显为至高！这样，我们就唱诗，歌颂你的大能。
verses.en: Rise up, O Lord, in strength![NOTE:1] We will sing and praise[NOTE:2] your power.
notes: Heb “with your bowstrings you fix against their faces,” i.e., “you fix your arrows on the bowstrings to shoot at them.”
Heb “in your strength,” but English idiom does not require the pronoun.sn The psalm concludes with a petition to the Lord, asking him to continue to intervene in strength for the king and nation.
verses.commentary:
21:13 This verse concludes the Psalm with
commanded praises of YHWH.

- Be exalted – BDB 926, KB 1202, Qal IMPERATIVE,
cf. 2 Sam. 22:47; Ps. 18:46; 46:10; 57:5,11; 108:5

- We will sing – BDB 1010, KB 1479, Qal COHORTATIVE

- We will praise – BDB 274, KB 273, Piel COHORTATIVE

▣ "Your strength" This
mantra begins the Psalm (cf. Ps. 21:1) and closes (cf. Ps. 21:13) the
Psalm. God is the chief character of the Bible. It is His book; it is
about Him!

PARAGRAPH LEVEL

This is a study guide commentary which means
that you are responsible for your own interpretation of the Bible. Each of
us must walk in the light we have. You, the Bible, and the Holy Spirit are
priority in interpretation. You must not relinquish this to a commentator.

Read the chapter in one sitting. Identify the subjects (reading cycle #3).
Compare your subject divisions with the five translations above.
Paragraphing is not inspired, but it is the key to following the original
author's intent, which is the heart of interpretation. Every paragraph has
one and only one subject.

CONTEXTUAL INSIGHTS

- Psalm 20 and 21 may be connected. Psalm 20 is the liturgical prayer for victory in battle and Psalm 21
is a liturgical welcoming of the King and soldiers home in victory. There are several Psalms in this first book of
the Psalms (Psalm 1-41) that deal with this theme. See Introduction to the Psalms, VI. B.

- Notice the possible strophes. By comparing the strophe divisions from various English translations
a person can ascertain how many main truths are expressed in a psalm.

- NASB – 2

- NKJV – 5

- NRSV – 4

- NJB – 6

Obviously it is difficult to be certain of how to identify strophes. There is often no textual marker.
Modern students must

- check the parallelism

- check the Hebrew beat pattern

- check related subject matter (every strophe has one major subject)
